references.text: Moses gave the same instructions to the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh that their wives, children, and livestock should remain in the land east of the Jordan, while the men were to cross over to help the other tribes.
The tribes of Reuben and Gad promised Moses that they would cross the Jordan armed ahead of their brothers and not return until the conquest was completed.
Moses repeats the command that the Transjordanian tribes must cross over armed ahead of their brothers, while wives, children, and livestock remain in the land Moses gave them.
Fulfillment of the promise: The men of Reuben, Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh crossed the Jordan armed ahead of the Israelites, about 40,000 fighting men.
Joshua sends the Transjordanian tribes back to their inheritance after they have fulfilled their duty to help their brothers take possession of Canaan.
The background for this arrangement: Reuben and Gad asked to receive the land east of the Jordan as their inheritance because of their large herds.
